info.title: workharbor API
info.description: The JSON API of `whr serve` (design §9.7). Served only on a unix socket, `api.sock` in the state directory (D29, §7.5), never on a network address; every route needs the bearer token. Responses are wrapped in the envelope of §9.2. Free text from agents, repositories and the forge (input, subject, message) is untrusted data.

servers.description: The unix socket api.sock in the supervisor's state directory; the host name is ignored.

default.description: An error. The HTTP status follows the exit code: 400 usage (2), 401 auth (4), 404 not found (3), 409 conflict or needs human (5, 6), 504 timeout (7), 500 other.

post.description: The kill switch (design §7.7). It needs `{"confirm": true}`, goes on after a failure, and lists what failed in `problems`. It cannot revoke the agent's own credentials. The attempt is an audit entry whatever happened.

get.description: Previews of dev servers that agents run in their environments (D33). A preview lives only in memory: it ends with its environment, after 12 hours and when the supervisor restarts. No secret is in the list.

post.summary: Open a preview of a port of a task's environment
post.description: The port must be one the repository's environment declares (forwardPorts or customizations.workharbor.previewPorts, read from the default branch) and the environment must be running. The answer carries a link that opens the preview in a browser once, for five minutes; a second request returns the preview already open with a new link. Not idempotent on purpose: a stored answer would keep a link.

url.description: The link; it carries a single-use grant, so treat it like a one-time password.

post.summary: Another link for an open preview
post.description: A link works once and for five minutes.

delete.description: Its listener, its connections and its token end at once.

post.summary: Make a one-time link that enrols a passkey
post.description: For the host's CLI only: the web UI cannot enrol a passkey. The link works once, for 5 minutes, and carries a secret token, so it is not stored for replay and the call takes no idempotency key.

delete.description: By its ID or a unique prefix. Revoking the last passkey turns the web sign-in back to the API token.

post.description: A hard interrupt (D11): the agent process is stopped, the run becomes paused, the questions and approvals it raised are superseded, and the environment keeps running.

post.summary: Resume a paused run from the agent's session
post.description: Relaunches the agent with the supervisor's briefing (D27). Refused while a login or quota question of the run is open.

get.summary: What a purge of the task's transcript would delete

post.description: Keeps the audit entries, usage rows and Decisions, and writes one audit entry for the purge. Refused while the task's run is running, and without {"confirm": true}.

get.summary: Totals of what the agents reported

default.description: An error. The HTTP status follows the exit code: 400 usage (2), 401 auth (4), 404 not found (3), 409 conflict or needs human (5, 6), 504 timeout (7), 500 other.

get.description: The tokens, the cost and the number of turns the agents reported, grouped, from the audit entries (design §5.7). A row is one group and one auth mode, so the notional cost of a subscription is never added to the spend of an API key; a turn without tokens or without a cost is counted, not read as zero. `windows` are the account's own usage windows and `balance` the latest balance the agent reported, if it reported one.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: The first request with a key runs; the same key and request returns the stored response (header Idempotent-Replay: true); the same key with another request is a conflict.

input_truncated.description: The input is cut: it is only the start of what the agent asked for, and an allow allows all of it.

run_id.description: absent when the task is held

held.description: true when the issue's author is not trusted: nothing was started and decision_id is a question for the human (start or cancel)

path.description: an empty folder below a workspace root

source.description: a repository path or an https URL

role.description: the agent whose branch to open; empty means the workspace's only agent

warnings.description: files in the copy that an editor may act on by itself; untrusted text

port.description: The app's port in the environment.

listen_port.description: The loopback port the preview listens on: the origin's port, which the forwarder maps.
